name: Mendoza

known.via: English Wikipedia "Mendoza wine region" (redirects to "Mendoza wine")

keyfacts: Mendoza, in the eastern foothills of the Andes, holds about 71% of Argentina's vineyard area and made about 81% of its wine in 2024.
Luján de Cuyo is one of Argentina's two Denominaciones de Origen Controladas, recognized nationally in 2005, and Malbec covers nearly 60% of its vineyards.
The climate is continental and semi-desert, and the main climate risks are hail, early or late frost and the hot, dry Zonda wind.
Soils are young alluvial and colluvial mixes of stones, clay, silt and sand, low in organic matter, and irrigation water comes mostly from Andean snowmelt rivers and aquifers.

notes: Mendoza's high-altitude districts of Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley are the source of Argentina's most highly rated Malbec.

blurb.text: Argentina's dominant wine region, making around three-quarters of the country's wine. Vineyards sit high in the eastern foothills of the Andes, and Malbec is the leading grape.
